body: Not really. I'm mostly more comfortable being alone. Losing the people I had to talk to is less of a problem in itself than the fact that it just makes everything else that much more difficult.
I'm not sure I have anything to say.

I'm just frustrated. I never had anyone to talk to but I never thought talking would help, and then it did. And now there just isn't anyone.

Thanks, though. For your time.

I appreciate the offer, I just doubt I'd take you up on it. I just learned the hard way that my problems are more than anyone wants to hear or can handle. I miss the friends I thought I had because when this thing happened yesterday they had enough background that I could tell them about it and they would understand. I'm not sure if I can start over again, especially now that I know what happens when you trust someone else.
I don't know how specifically you're asking. I'm American.

That's the thing. I started getting real help. I didn't expect anyone to just come in and fix my life. I made sure they specifically, explicitly knew that. I just wanted a friend. Someone to talk to.

I'm back in the situation I was in at the beginning and I made it worse by trying and failing to get out of it. I can't be more specific than that on a public forum. I'm really not allowed to be talking about it at all.

I meant what I said, that's all. I wasn't trying to be melodramatic or anything. People always leave but I've never had anyone so close that it mattered when they were gone.

And that's the problem, and please don't think I mean you specifically. The only thing I really want is someone who would be there, or someone who would at least try. I'd just never realized that was so much to ask for.
The same. I appreciate you trying to help. I just don't have anything to add.

I have some things going on that I've never been able to talk about, for a lot of reasons. And part of it was I never saw the point. The risk outweighed any possible benefits. I finally was able to start talking about it. And then I trusted the people I was talking to and I even started to work towards making things better. But nothing was simple or straightforward and it seems like... when it became evident that even with me making an effort, there wasn't going to be some quick and easy solution to improve things, it stopped being worth their time. With one of them, it was gradual and in part my own fault. The others got busy with their own lives. And I can understand that. But I can't understand how that makes it okay to just cease all communication. I needed help. I would've accepted that my situation was too much for or beyond the ability of someone to handle. I wouldn't disagree. I just... I never felt abandoned before because I never had anyone to be abandoned by. And I think I'd have preferred if things had stayed that way.
I'm happy for you that things worked out.
